items.prompt: Is the excavation shored or braced, sloped to the angle of repose, or in stable material with the competent person's written permission?
Is the shoring or bracing strong enough to support the sides of the excavation?
Are loads, material, plant and equipment kept away from the edge, or the sides supported against them?
Where the excavation could affect an adjoining building, structure or road, has it been made stable?
Is there a safe means of access within six metres of everyone working in the excavation?
Have electricity, water, gas and similar services been located and made safe?
Where the public or a road is near, is there a barrier or fence at least one metre high, with warning lights or markers at night or in poor visibility?
Are the confined-space precautions of the General Safety Regulations followed by everyone entering?
Are warning signs placed next to the excavation where people are working or doing inspections or tests?

title: Construction vehicle and mobile plant pre-use inspection

items.prompt: Is the vehicle or plant in good working order?
Is the operator trained, certified competent, carrying proof of competency and authorised in writing?
Does the operator have a medical certificate of fitness for this vehicle or plant (Annexure 3)?
Is there a safe and suitable way to get on and off?
Is edge protection in place where it could fall into an excavation, water or a lower area?
Is the operator protected from falling material and from being crushed if it overturns?
Does the operator's warning hooter work?
Does the automatic reversing alarm work?
Where visibility needs extra lighting, are at least two headlights and two taillights working?
Are temporary works operations supervised by a competent person appointed in writing?
Is the structure properly erected, supported and braced, with no loads beyond its design?
Is the structure built to the structural design drawings?
Are the activity-specific temporary works drawings kept on site?
Was the equipment examined and checked for suitability by a competent person before use?
Has the competent person given written authorisation before any concrete is cast?
Has any damaged or weakened part been removed or reinforced?
Are deck panels secured against displacement?
Are measures in place to stop people slipping where release agents have been applied?
Is the structure staying in place until the concrete is strong enough and the competent person has authorised removal in writing?
Are the foundation conditions suitable for the loads in the temporary works design?
Have electrical cables and apparatus under, over or on the site been identified and guarded against?
Are the electrical installations and machinery strong enough for site conditions?
Is control of the temporary electrical installations given to a competent person appointed in writing?
Are materials and equipment properly stored?
Are scrap, waste and debris being removed?
Are access routes, exits and passageways clear of materials?
Are materials no longer needed being removed instead of piling up?
Is waste only dropped from height through a chute that meets reg 14(6)?
In a built-up area next to a public way, is the site fenced with controlled access points?
Where work is overhead, is there a catch platform or net, or is the danger area fenced off?
Are adequate storage areas provided?
Are storage areas demarcated?
Are storage areas neat and under control?
